dt_fine <- 0.001
set.seed(131)
W_fine <- c(0, cumsum(sigma * sqrt(dt_fine) * rnorm(3000)))   # noise added up, at 1 ms resolution

# The same trial with steps of length dt_step: the evidence at the end of each step
step_path <- function(dt_step) {
  m   <- round(dt_step / dt_fine)
  idx <- seq(1, length(W_fine), by = m)
  t   <- (idx - 1) * dt_fine
  X   <- z * a + v * t + W_fine[idx]           # start + drift so far + noise so far
  hit <- which(X >= a | X <= 0)[1]             # first step at or past a boundary
  list(t = t[1:hit], X = X[1:hit], dt = dt_step)
}
p50 <- step_path(0.05)
p10 <- step_path(0.01)
p1  <- step_path(0.001)

text:
lower boundary, \(\sigma = 1\) decision time \(t = \text{RT} - T_{er}\):\[
f_{\text{lower}}(t \mid v, , z)
= \frac{1}{^2}\, \exp\!\left(-v z - \frac{v^2 t}{2}\right)\, g\!\left(\frac{t}{^2} \,\middle|\, z\right)
\]\(1/^2\) factor \(t/^2\) argument rescale time process boundary

process drift boundary 1. \(g\) closed form. Navarro & Fuss
(2009) give two series :\[
g_{\text{small}}(u \mid z) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi u^3}} \sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} (z + 2k)\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{(z+2k)^2}{2u}\right)
\]\[

\]first series converges quickly small \(u\) second large \(u\),

# Density g(u | z) for a process with no drift and a boundary at 1.
g_std <- function(u, z, K = 10) {
  out <- numeric(length(u))               # density is effectively 0 for u near 0
  small <- u < 1 & u > 1e-8
  if (any(small)) {                       # small-time series, k = -K..K
    zz <- outer(z[small], 2 * (-K:K), "+")
    out[small] <- rowSums(zz * exp(-zz^2 / (2 * u[small]))) / sqrt(2 * pi * u[small]^3)
  }
  large <- u >= 1
  if (any(large)) {                       # large-time series, k = 1..K
    k <- 1:K
    terms <- exp(-outer(u[large], k^2) * pi^2 / 2) * sin(outer(z[large], k) * pi)
    out[large] <- pi * as.vector(terms %*% k)
  }
  out
}

# Density of each trial's response and RT. Every parameter can be given as one
# value per trial, which is what trial-level models need (Part 2).
ddm_density <- function(rt, upper, v, a, z, t0) {
  n <- length(rt)
  upper <- rep_len(upper, n); v <- rep_len(v, n); a <- rep_len(a, n)
  z <- rep_len(z, n); t0 <- rep_len(t0, n)
  t <- rt - t0
  dens <- numeric(n)
  ok <- t > 0                             # no response is possible before t0
  vv <- ifelse(upper, -v, v)              # upper boundary: reverse the drift
  zz <- ifelse(upper, 1 - z, z)           # and mirror the starting point
  dens[ok] <- exp(-vv[ok] * a[ok] * zz[ok] - vv[ok]^2 * t[ok] / 2) / a[ok]^2 *
              g_std(t[ok] / a[ok]^2, zz[ok])
  dens
}

fit_rdm <- function(data, n_starts = 5) {
  min_rt <- min(data$rt)
  starts <- cbind(c(log(1.5), 0, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5),
                  replicate(n_starts - 1, c(log(runif(1, 0.8, 2.5)), rnorm(1, 0, 0.3),
                                            rnorm(1, 0, 1), runif(3, 0, 2))))
  fits <- apply(starts, 2, function(s)
    optim(s, neg_loglik_u, data = data, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 1000)))
  best <- fits[[which.min(sapply(fits, `[[`, "value"))]]
  list(u = best$par, par = to_natural(best$par, min_rt), logLik = -best$value,
       converged = best$convergence == 0)
}

# Simulate the same trials n_rep times from a set of fitted values
simulate_from_fit <- function(par, data, n_rep = 20) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(n_rep), function(r) {
    v <- make_drift(par[4:6], data$coherence, data$direction)
    s <- ddm_sample(v, par[["a"]], par[["z"]], par[["t0"]])
    tibble(coherence = data$coherence, direction = data$direction, upper = s$upper, rt = s$rt)
  }) |>
    mutate(correct = as.integer(upper == (direction == "right")))
}

# For each coherence level and correct/error: how often, and the RT quantiles
summarise_cells <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(coherence) |>
    mutate(n_coherence = n()) |>
    group_by(coherence, correct) |>
    reframe(prop = n() / first(n_coherence),
            quantile = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9),
            rt = quantile(rt, quantile))
}

set.seed(2)
cells <- bind_rows(
